references.text: Joshua takes over leadership after Moses' death, and the text confirms that Moses, the servant of the Lord, is dead.
Moses is referred to as 'the servant of the Lord', the same title used in Deuteronomy 34:5.
The Lord tells Moses that he will die on the mountain because he is not allowed to enter the Promised Land, which is fulfilled in Deuteronomy 34:5.
God commands Moses to go up Mount Nebo in the land of Moab to see the land of Canaan before he dies there.
The Lord tells Moses that his day of death is approaching, a prediction fulfilled in chapter 34.
God says that Moses will not lead the people into the land because of his disobedience at Meribah, which explains why he dies in Moab.
Moses is described as a faithful servant in God's house, the same servant title used for Moses at his death.
Refers to a dispute between the archangel Michael and the devil over Moses' body, connecting to his death and burial.
